Pages 4 and 5 were photographed twice in the first copy; they are given once.
The tissue guard over the frontispiece was not transcribed.
The chapters have numbers and printed summaries but no titles; the short titles in the contents (the places of each chapter) are the editor’s.

In most Swedish names the printer set an o with a ring above (o̊: Hango̊, Lo̊nnrot, Ho̊gholmen) where Swedish has ö; the edition keeps it as printed. A true ö appears in a few names (Borgström, Hangö in one caption).

summary: An account of a summer journey through Finland, then a grand duchy of the Russian Empire, by a Finnish-born writer publishing in English as “Paul Waineman”. The tour begins at Helsingfors (Helsinki) and goes by steamer, canal, rail, and cart to Borgå, Viborg, the falls of Imatra, Sordavala and Lake Ladoga, Nyslott, Kuopio, and Kajana; down the rapids of the Uleå River to Uleåborg; north to Torneå on the Swedish border; and back south by Tammerfors and Tavastehus to Åbo, the country houses of the south-west, and Hangö. Along the way the author describes towns, castles, inns and railways, farm life, wedding customs, the Kalevala and its singers, Finnish painters, and recent history. The book has 16 colour plates after paintings by Alexander Federley and 16 other plates.
